title: Clean FIO composition and transport with derivative loss
source_hypothesis: Fixed 1/2<rho<=1 and delta=1-rho. Real homogeneous canonical relations with full cotangent closure and no zero-component axes; proper actual kernel supports and proper clean matching to a fixed embedded image. Scalar transport allows nonproper A, but P is proper on half-densities, with chosen homogeneous principal p vanishing on the projected relation and ordinary remainders through order s-2.
completed_component_scope: General-rho kernel maps, antidual adjoints, clean composition, actual product limits, all symbol remainders, ordered fiber densities and the scalar transport theorem with exact m+s-rho order, m+s-2rho full-graph error and intrinsic epsilon quotient.
reviewed_arguments: Kernel correspondence, strong topologies and wavefront action use exactly the established axis-free kernel hypotheses. General-symbol phase estimates supply them, with uniform smooth-input truncation bounds.
Adjoints retain antidual bundles, both swapped cotangent factors, Gaussian/Maslov conjugation and the complete general-rho symbol class and remainder.
Clean geometry retains actual embeddedness, proper cotangent matching, submersion and fixed excess. The full proper-connected criterion is reused; proper base support is a separate condition.

Unequal phase frequencies are discarded only after full transposed integration in the middle base. Each step gains rho. Negative individual orders, all coefficient derivatives and every output derivative are explicitly controlled.

Comparable amplitudes become joint symbols only after the ratio cutoff. The middle variable v=R y gives exact Jacobian R-to-the-minus-nY, with every frequency derivative gaining rho through the complete chain rule.
The summed phase has the actual clean critical equations, correct external covectors and exact excess. Dimension arithmetic gives m1+m2+e/2, and the sole Gaussian factor is (2pi)^(-e/2).

Smooth frequency truncations converge both as oscillatory distributions and as operators on compact smooth inputs. Uniform seminorms and common supports identify the actual product, not a formal product of singular kernels.

Global assembly uses both base properness and cotangent properness. Finite matching covers, complementary smoothing, closed projected kernel supports and both proper output/input projections are proved.

The exact linear density/Maslov map gives ordered finite bundle coefficients and a fiber density. Compact submersion charts prove every output symbol seminorm; every normal remainder drops epsilon and representative changes are controlled.

Scalar transport retains a homogeneous principal symbol, ordinary first remainder and full second-order error. Scalar half-density subprincipal invariance also allows an ordinary first remainder without a full classical expansion.
Separate base coordinate changes preserve which variable P acts on. The exact frequency normal form and actual full left symbol justify Taylor division and the integrated principal amplitude.
The improved restriction proof uses ordinary base coefficients times a frequency-only S_rho symbol. Its rho gain gives the full three-term table, with the true graph error m+s-2rho.

Fixed-base and total graph derivatives are compared explicitly. The identities S+T=div F and S-T=sum p_xxi give the exact half-divergence and subprincipal coefficient, including complex principal symbols.

The actual product order is m+s-rho. The intrinsic symbol formula is correctly stated modulo the epsilon quotient; the stronger full-graph remainder is not assigned to an arbitrary principal representative.

The xDx conormal-point example attains the enlarged transport order and checks both half contributions. The exact product of two oscillatory pseudodifferential symbols attains the epsilon drop; all proper-localization tails are explicitly rapid.
A genuine compact-circle clean fiber has excess one, input orders minus one quarter, output order zero and noncommuting matrix product E11/2. Its Gaussian factors cancel exactly once.

Thirty-five finite exact checks verify only the stated dimension, order, nonlinear graph/divergence, matrix and circle identities. The complete estimates and limiting arguments are written in the lesson.
All 373 formulas and 51 numbered displays parse. Eighteen overlapping desktop captures, the entire exact figure and two mobile samples were inspected; all display/figure extents remain accessible.

The approved source was read at printed 17–24 with exact file and page-text hashes. No source previews, backups, workers or messages were created. Continuity, the iterated criterion, the full source audit and external foundations remain active.
